If you find that you are not getting the results that you're expecting, there are several things you can do to get more flavor into your food. Try one or more of these and see if you notice a difference:

1. Grill at a lower temperature for a longer time. Smoking at 225 degrees and lower typically has the best results.
2. If your grill has an upper rack, try cooking food up top to allow more exposure to the smoke.
3. Experiment with different wood types. Some may provide a more noticeable flavor for different people.
4. If wrapping your food, sometimes using butcher paper instead of aluminum foil allows a stronger smoke flavor to get through.

We also have hundreds of recipes on Traeger.com that are specifically designed to get the most out of your smoker. Not only will you find more traditional cooks, like poultry, pork and beef, but you’ll also discover new ways to make to pies, casseroles and even ice cream that you never even imagined were possible. Whatever you feel like making, search through our recipes. You’ll be surprised what you can find.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hello, an thank you for providing your feedback on the Pro 780. Smoke coming out of the grease spout is nothing to be concerned about, but it shouldn’t be excessive or continuous throughout the cook. Typically, heavy smoke will only be produced when pellets are added to the fire. The rest of the time, the grill will be creating what is referred to as 'blue smoke', which is not very visible. Although seeing some smoke exiting through the spout is normal, the majority of it should still be coming from the chimney.

Excessive smoke from sections of the grill other than the chimney may indicate that there is an airflow problem. One of the main causes of this is a chimney cap that is set too low. While it might seem like the cap is made to be adjustable, it actually needs to have a ¾” gap at all times and should only be moved to take it off for cleaning inside the smokestack. When it is too low, air flow is restricted and the smoke will start finding other exits, such as the grease spout or even from around the lid. 

Another possible cause is the foil on the tray. This may not be related to your situation, but if foil is wrapped too loosely, it can also have an impact on the airflow. This may cause a variety of problems, including excess smoke from the spout to improper grease flow to the bucket. While it is recommended that you use the drip tray liners that are designed specifically for your model, foil is acceptable, but it needs to be wrapped tight enough that it doesn’t alter the space taken up by the tray, and also be flat enough on top to avoid hindering proper grease flow. 

Although you have apparently called us once before, it may be worth contacting us again. If we haven’t done this already, an agent can use the camera on your phone to look over your grill with you and see if anything can be adjusted. You can reach us up until 10:00 PM MST, every day of the year.

Results.ReviewText: I have an earlier version of this grill that doesn’t have wheels on two of the legs by the handle.  It has all the Wi-Fi features that this one has though and looks identical otherwise.  I bought this one because our old We’ll loved Traeger got knocked over and damaged.  The new one was purchased in 2019 from Home Depot and I still have it and use it only occasionally now.  There are two issues that make this grill not as good as our old one that got damaged.  That old grill made absolutely the best grilled chicken on the planet.  When the fat from the chicken dripped off on to the foil lined drip pan, it would bathe the chicken in wet steam when it it hit the drip pan which keeps the chicken moist and crisps up the skin perfectly.  As this occurred, more smoke would develop and exhaust out of the chimney.  The issue with this one is that the overwhelmingly vast majority of smoke always comes out of the outlet where the grease trap is.  The chimney has virtually no smoke when it operates which is completely different from our older one!  I called Traeger to discuss this issue and was actually told it wasn’t a problem!  The chicken on the new one is nowhere near as good as the old one and imparts little to no smoke flavor.  In addition, the drip bucket doesn’t catch near the same amount of grease as our old one.  In fact, I have only had to empty the drip bucket once since I’ve had it and I have no idea why it is so radically different than the old one.  The second problem is that the old drip pan showed virtually no signs of rusting over a lot of years of use while the new one shows tons of rust every time I change the foil out that protects the pan.    Both were always kept in my garage and only rolled out when I wanted to use it.  Overall, the new one doesn’t perform nearly as well as the old one.  And with all Traegers, they never get hot enough to produce a decent sear even though the temperature read out says it gets to 500.  Simply put, the one I have won’t hardly sear anything and I’m very disappointed because my older one produced way better cooking results.

ClientResponses.Response: Although 5.0 GHz provides a faster connection, Traegers use 2.4 GHz due to the frequency’s longer range. Since there is only a minimal amount of data that needs to be transmitted, high speed is not a priority, whereas increasing the distance that the grill can be from the router provides more freedom to position it in an ideal location. However, it is very uncommon for a WiFi router to be exclusively 5.0 GHz. In most cases, they are dual band, which allows either frequency to be used depending on the device and sometimes creating a dedicated 2.4 GHz guest network is all that is needed to bypass any issues. If you are not sure how to do this, your ISP should be able to assist with setting it up. If you still need some help after that, you can always call our support line at 1-800-TRAEGER.

Hi, and thanks for leaving your feedback on the Pro 780. Although we can expect some variation in temperature, it should not be excessive. There are specific things that may cause this, such as very large pans, drip trays wrapped loosely in foil or damage to internal components. None of these may be the case in your situation, but are still worth pointing out. 

Even with the larger grills, you really shouldn’t have to cook higher to get the same results. One thing that is easy to check is the initial temperature reading on a cold grill. This should always be within about 20 degrees of the ambient air temperature and anything more than that is worth calling in to us for at 1-800-TRAEGER. 

In regard to the insulation blanket, it is better to use it only in certain situations, as they are not designed for cooking at higher than 350º or if the weather is above 30º. Beyond these ranges can have an effect on performance and possibly cause damage to the grill or blanket. 

As for using the WiFi, that is definitely one of the key features of your Pro 780. Hopefully, you can try it before purchasing a replacement grill, even if just to keep tabs on the temperature from inside a warm house on a cold winter day. Should you need help connecting it, this is only one of the many topics that our agents are trained to assist with. 

I want to thank you again for posting. We are always interested in what our customers have to say, and it also helps others make informed decisions.

Results.ReviewText:
I've had my 780 grill for about 10 months and use it a minimum of 3 times per week. Previously I had a Traeger Bronson for 5 years and wanted to upgrade. I have to admit the 780 is bigger than I need, and at that time I should have purchased the 575, but here are my findings after cooking on the 780 over 120 times so far. 
The right side and across the front area of the grill are every large areas of cold spots. The biscuit test proved to me that these areas are not prime for maintaining high enough temps. I don't know if the firepot is just not adequate enough to heat the entire area or what might be the answer. Maybe relocating the firepot closer to the right side so that heat spreads across the grill better, to the chimney on the left?
I don't use the wifi option so I can't comment on that. It's just not an important upgrade for me. 
I believe it's because of the large interior space, but none-the-less I've had to increase the temp by anywhere from 25-50 degrees and/or increase the cook times in order to get the same results for many of my routine recipes.
The firepot itself collects ash more readily than my previous Traeger, instead of blowing  the ash into the cavity below the drip tray, causing me to vacuum it out far more often, and causing the grill to heat more slowly, when the firepot is so full of ash, after only short a short time prior to the previous vacuuming.
Because of the large amount of air cavity, it uses far more pellets than my previous Traeger in order to keep that much area at, or close to, the set temp, even though I have an insulation blanket on it year round.
Where the grease flows down into the trough is a much bigger pain in the neck to clean out than the Gen 1 Traegers.
Although it's not a big deal, I'm not a fan of the on/off switch, then setting the temp, plus then pushing the ignite button. The gen 1 Traeger's are easier and faster to start than the Gen 2, in my opinion.
All that said, I'm going to purchase a Pro 22 in the Spring when they run their first seasonal sale, that way the savings will pay for a front tray and part of the cost of a cover. I'll also purchase an insulation blanket because I grill a lot during the cold months and it's a great addition for Winter cooking. 
I'm going back to a smaller grill, because it suits my needs better, and I'm going back to a Gen 1 grill because I like to controller system better for me personally.
Some of my findings are strictly personal, and may be no problem for others, but it never hurts for a company like Traeger to get constructive feedback, no matter what it might be.
I would not buy another brand of pellet grill because I truly feel Traeger is a quality company that produces some great quality items. I hope my comments help some of you who are on the fence and are also helpful to Traeger.

I've had a mixed experience with my Traeger over the last year and a half. When using it at low to mid temperatures, I've been able to achieve a nice bark and smoke flavor on my pork and brisket, and the ease of use is a plus.

However, I wouldn't say that the Traeger is a jack-of-all-trades grill like it's advertised. While it can reach temperatures up to 500 degrees, it requires meticulous cleaning beforehand to avoid grease fire, which can melt the powder coat off of the grill. Additionally, the amount of pellets and time it takes to reach high temperatures is not very efficient.

In my experience, the Traeger is best used as a smoker rather than an all-purpose grill. All of the people I know who own a Traeger also own another grill, including myself. 

One issue that I've encountered is the quality of the powder coat. After experiencing a grease fire because I missed one spot in the grill when cleaning, the coat bubbled and flaked off, which is unacceptable. I'm not the only one in my Traeger circle who has experienced this issue, so it's something to keep in mind.

Results.ReviewText: Got this as an early christmas gift from the wife. Picked it up Dec. 8th. Used it that day, worked great. Tried to start it up christmas eve - blinking power switch. Doesn't turn on, completely useless. Customer service was great the first go around. Video called me to trouble shoot - sent me a new power brick, harness and switch. Got it today, replaced, still nothing. Waited 25ish minutes for the customer service rep to pick up and make me go through the same song and dance - tried to tell me it was the power cord. I convinced her to video call me again that night so I can show her the power cord hooked up  to a multimeter showing correct voltage. Theyre now going to send me a new control panel. Almost had to do this for a third time. I wish I went with another brand...all I want to do is grill - and I cant. Had it for almost a month, worked once. Really disappointing because i've wanted one for so long.
